# Milestone brief — ui-uplift-m10

**Title:** Style Discover results; close the last unstyled classes
**Kind:** milestone
**Roadmap:** ui-uplift (plans/ui-uplift/roadmap.yaml)
**Status:** planned
**Lane:** now
**Target:** 2026-08-20 -> 2026-08-27

## Parent epic

- ui-uplift-e2 — Finish debt — every server-emitted class ships with its CSS rule
  Four class families shipped with zero CSS rule anywhere in the stylesheet. The root cause the current-state critic traced nearly every HIGH finding to: feature milestones shipped complete, tested, secure behaviour and left CSS as an afterthought scoped to "does it render", not "does it look finished" — because no milestone's acceptance criteria ever said "style this". This epic closes the backlog AND lands the standing rule as a derived test so it cannot regenerate.

## Summary

UPL-9. Five emitted classes with zero CSS rules. This is the ONLY surface in the console that presents external content for operator judgment and it is the least-styled thing in the product — a bare bulleted list with default browser margins. Give it a bibliography-style title/meta/abstract hierarchy. SCOPE EXPANDED 2026-08-04 by ui-uplift-m9 finding M8: four further emitted classes have zero CSS and no owning milestone anywhere in this roadmap — `status-badge__remediation` (server/routes/ui.py:336) and the three `topic-block` / `topic-category` / `topic-description` classes (server/routes/notebooks.py:621-623). They were parked in the m9 coverage test's `_KNOWN_UNSTYLED` deferral list, which is a holding pen, not a home. Folding them in here means m10 empties that list entirely and the BAN-R2 coverage policy binds unconditionally from then on — the epic's actual finish line.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Given a discovery run returning candidates, when rendered, then title, meta and abstract are typographically distinguished and candidates are separated
2. Given the meta line, then it uses --mono and inherits tabular-nums
3. Given the results group, then NO fade-in keyframe is added — globalViewTransitions already crossfades that swap at 200ms and a second animation would double-animate
4. Given a relevance line, then it is only added if the arXiv Atom driver genuinely supplies the basis; a manufactured reason violates operational honesty
5. Given the remediation block emitted at server/routes/ui.py:336, then `.status-badge__remediation` has a CSS rule in app.css
6. Given the topic fragment at server/routes/notebooks.py:621-623, then `.topic-block`, `.topic-category` and `.topic-description` each have a CSS rule in app.css
7. Given this milestone is complete, then `_KNOWN_UNSTYLED` in tests/test_ui_class_css_coverage.py is EMPTY and every emitted class is covered by a real rule rather than a deferral
8. Given app.css grows past the line cap asserted in test_ui_m3/m4/m5 (480 at 2026-08-04, with app.css already at 460), then the cap is raised deliberately in all three sibling tests in the same commit — not worked around by writing denser CSS
